name: PCF8523 real-time clock breakout
description: NXP PCF8523 real-time clock/calendar: seconds to years in BCD with leap-year handling, minute/hour/day/weekday alarm, two timers, offset calibration, battery switch-over with low-battery flag and a programmable open-drain square-wave output (32.768 kHz to 1 Hz), on a 400 kHz I2C bus at address 0x68. Chip runs on 1.6-5.5 V with I2C active (1.8 V with battery switch-over) and draws about 1.2 uA timekeeping. Sold as: Adafruit PCF8523 Real Time Clock Breakout Board - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 5189) (5-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, SQW plus two STEMMA QT sockets; 10 kOhm I2C pull-ups to VIN, power LED, 32.768 kHz crystal, CR1220 holder, no regulator), I2C address 0x68.
eli5: A tiny clock that keeps the date and time, even while your board is switched off if a coin cell is fitted.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3-5 V straight to the chip (no regulator) and to the 10 kOhm I2C pull-ups: use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, up to 400 kHz (1 MHz chip max). 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data. 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board

pins.name: SQW
pins.description: INT1/CLKOUT: square wave (32.768 kHz at power-on) or alarm interrupt (active LOW). Open-drain with no pull-up on the board: add one (e.g. Pin.PULL_UP or 10 kOhm) if used. Not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: Adafruit PCF8523 RTC breakout STEMMA QT 5189
buildNotes: Fixed I2C address 0x68 (D0h write / D1h read), the same as a DS1307/DS3231, so only one of these per bus.
Header order on the board (silkscreen, left to right): VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, SQW. The two STEMMA QT sockets carry GND, VIN, SDA, SCL.
SCL and SDA are pulled up to VIN with 10 kOhm on the board: power VIN from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico so the bus never sees 5 V.
Read or write all seven time registers (03h-09h) in one burst finished within 1 s; the chip blocks its counters during the access.
Bit 7 of the seconds register (OS) is set at power-up and whenever the oscillator stopped: the time is invalid until you set it. Setting the time clears it.
Battery switch-over is OFF at power-on (Control_3 PM = 111), so the CR1220 is not used until you write PM = 000; the driver does this whenever it sets the time.
SQW is open-drain with no pull-up on the board and outputs 32.768 kHz from power-up; write COF = 111 (register 0Fh bits 5-3) to switch it off, which also frees the pin for the alarm interrupt.
The PCF8523 is not temperature compensated: expect a drift of up to about 2 s per day (use the Offset register 0Eh to trim).

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf8523 import PCF8523

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
rtc = PCF8523(i2c)
rtc.datetime((2028, 2, 28, 23, 59, 57))  # Monday 28 Feb 2028 (leap year), 23:59:57
while True:
    y, mo, d, wd, h, mi, s = rtc.datetime()
    print('wd=%d %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d' % (wd, y, mo, d, h, mi, s))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Keeps the time it was set to and rolls from 28 Feb into 29 Feb 2028 (leap year)
